family.description: Exploratory pilot of issue 8e53235b, protocol version 4: this addendum is the pilot and every cell is exploratory. Question: does placing each systematic codeword of a packed binary BCH batch encode by a word copy of the message and a shifted placement of the parity, in place of one bit write per coordinate, make the whole batch consumer faster? Both arms are the one executable consumer-arm of the bit-storage consumer harness, built once from one tree; the environment selects the route. Both arms call BchCode::encode_batch_into or, in a family-pinned cell, encode_batch_family_into, on the same messages with a workspace and an output the caller prepared, so message packing, the reduction, the codeword assembly and the output are inside the timed call. The baseline workspace keeps CodewordAssembly::BitSerial, the assembly every encode selects, which is the pinned pre-change consumer; the candidate workspace selects CodewordAssembly::WordWise. The pair differs in that selection alone. The harness's consumer-verify requires every family under both assemblies to write the reference family's bits. The declared cells reach the mother code of the DVB-T2 short frame, GF(2^14) of mother-code length 16383 and designed distance 25; the mother code of the DVB-T2 normal frame, GF(2^16) of mother-code length 65535 and designed distance 25; and the degree-8 mother code of corpus row B3, GF(2^8) of mother-code length 255 and designed distance 9. Cells: the deciding cell is the 256-message batch on the short-frame mother code through the family the production dispatcher selects, the consumer the 04b85d10 profile ranks, with the improvement objective. Four non-regression cells guard it: the same batch on the normal-frame mother code, where the codeword is four times as long; the short-frame batch with the carry-less-multiply fold family pinned and with the bit-sliced interleaved family pinned, the registered families a profile can admit in place of the reference; and one message on the degree-8 mother code, where the assembly has the least to place and a fixed per-call cost shows most. Every cell is single-core and warm: the assembly runs on the calling thread and the batch's buffers are cache-resident between calls. Frozen confirmation selection: a first confirmatory attempt spends alpha/2 = 0.025, and P-20's tail-support bound, 10000 * (0.025 / m) / 2 >= 20, admits m = 6 confirmatory comparisons, so the confirmation retains all five cells. Frozen resolution rule: the canonical freezer's, the widest relative bootstrap half-width over every pilot cell, rounded up to two decimals. Frozen decision rule: the word-wise assembly is adopted as the one assembly of the packed kernel when the confirmation's receipt is accepted and every confirmatory cell records pass, which is improvement on the deciding cell and non-regression on each guard; on any other recorded outcome the bit-serial assembly is retained and the candidate is removed. A pilot whose deciding cell places the candidate behind the baseline is a recorded no-win without a confirmation. The rule reads the acceptance summary's recorded outcomes and nothing else.

effect.rationale: The bar of the bit-storage layout consumer family of issue 04b85d10, held for a change measured on the same whole consumer: ten percent of the whole batch encode, packing and output included, is the smallest gain worth a new bit-run primitive in the bit-storage crate and a second statement of the layout mapping in the packed kernel.
effect.equivalence_rationale: A guard cell records the candidate as not worse when it is at most five percent slower than the bit-serial assembly on the whole consumer, the equivalence margin of the bit-storage layout consumer family of issue 04b85d10 for the same consumer. The confirmation freezes a pilot-derived resolution strictly below this margin.
effect.material_gap_rationale: No cell is a comparator-gap cell: every cell compares two assemblies of one gf2 encode, so no material-gap threshold applies.

complexity_budget.maintenance_rationale: The adopted state is one safe bit-run write on BitVec in gf2-core and one assembly function in the packed BCH kernel of gf2-coding that replaces the bit-serial one, within 120 added nonblank production lines, with no unsafe kernel, no selector, no dependency and no second entry point. The CodewordAssembly selection and its workspace setter exist for the measurement and either outcome removes them.
